title: 2nd Stopping Place 5th Truth Universal And Particular Order And Wisdom Indicating An All Powerful All Wise One

questions.question: What main claim is made about the order found in everything from the universe down to the human body?
questions.answer: It shows that all things are arranged with deep wisdom and exact measure.

questions.question: Which two levels of creation are both mentioned to show that this order includes everything?
questions.answer: It includes both the very large, like the whole cosmos, and the very small, like details within the human body.

questions.question: What examples from human beings are given as signs of precise order?
questions.answer: The passage points to the human face, the senses in the head, and the movement of blood cells.

questions.question: According to the passage, who alone can truly act on things in an intentional and creative way?
questions.answer: Only the One who has absolute power and absolute wisdom can do that.

questions.question: How are created things described in relation to that divine action?
questions.answer: They are described as receiving what is done to them, showing what is manifested in them, and not acting independently.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect order with knowledge and wisdom?
questions.answer: Because arranging things for clear purposes and useful results requires understanding and wise planning.

questions.question: What else, besides knowledge and wisdom, is said to be necessary for such ordering?
questions.answer: Will and choice are also necessary.

questions.question: What does the regular and beneficial arrangement of the world prove about the Creator?
questions.answer: It proves that the Creator is one and acts with will and choice.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the relationship between divine power, will, and choice in bringing things into being?
questions.answer: Things are brought into existence by power, given their condition by will, and given their form by choice.

questions.question: What picture is used for the world in the third paragraph?
questions.answer: The world is pictured as a place that hosts living guests and provides for them.

questions.question: What do the repeated examples of “one” in that paragraph suggest?
questions.answer: They suggest that the One who manages and owns the world is also one.

questions.question: What two qualities of the Maker are highlighted through the image of hosting guests?
questions.answer: His generosity and His care for those He hosts are emphasized.

questions.question: What kinds of divine realities are listed in the fourth paragraph?
questions.answer: Divine Names, attributes, and actions are listed.

questions.question: What does the passage say about where those Names and actions are at work?
questions.answer: They are active everywhere throughout the world.

questions.question: How do the divine Names and actions relate to one another?
questions.answer: They support and complete one another in a deeply united way.

questions.question: What example is given to show several Names appearing together at once?
questions.answer: When life appears in a thing, creating, shaping, and providing also appear at the same time.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from the fact that the same comprehensive actions appear everywhere in the same system?
questions.answer: The One indicated by those Names and the Doer of those actions must be one, single, and unique.

questions.question: How does the passage end in terms of belief and response?
questions.answer: It ends with a clear statement of faith and acceptance of this truth.

questions.question: What idea opens the passage about everything in creation?
questions.answer: It opens by saying that all things contain a careful and wise arrangement.

questions.question: How does the passage use both the earth’s movements and the human body to support its point?
questions.answer: It uses them to show that the same kind of order appears in both the large world and the small details of life.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about any being other than Allah acting creatively on things?
questions.answer: It teaches that no other being can independently act on things with true creative intention.

questions.question: What does it mean when things are called passive in this passage?
questions.answer: It means they do not create or direct themselves but are acted upon.

questions.question: Why is purpose important in the argument of the second paragraph?
questions.answer: Because purposeful arrangement points to an aware and intentional maker rather than blind chance.

questions.question: What does usefulness in creation help prove according to the passage?
questions.answer: It helps prove that creation comes from wisdom and deliberate choice.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage draw from the varied but beneficial arrangement of the universe?
questions.answer: It concludes that the Creator of all beings is one and acts knowingly and willingly.

questions.question: What three stages are described in how things come to be what they are?
questions.answer: They come into existence through power, receive their state through will, and receive their form through choice.

questions.question: What metaphor is used to describe the world, and what does it suggest?
questions.answer: The world is described as a lodging place for guests, suggesting care, provision, and welcome.

questions.question: What is the effect of repeating many examples of oneness in the world?
questions.answer: It strengthens the conclusion that the One who runs the world must also be one.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the treatment of living beings in this world-hostel image?
questions.answer: It shows them being served and cared for through many means.

questions.question: What does the use of many servants or officials suggest about the Maker?
questions.answer: It suggests greatness, generosity, and authority.

questions.question: Which categories of divine reality are named together near the end of the passage?
questions.answer: The passage names divine Names, divine qualities, and divine acts.

questions.question: What is said about the reach of these Names and acts?
questions.answer: They extend everywhere and are present in every part of the world.

questions.question: How strongly connected are the divine Names described to be?
questions.answer: They are described as so closely connected that their effects seem united together.

questions.question: What happens when the Name related to giving life appears in something?
questions.answer: Other divine actions such as creating, shaping, and providing appear with it at the same time.

questions.question: What does the sameness of these actions everywhere prove?
questions.answer: It proves that their source and doer are one.

questions.question: What attitude toward this teaching is expressed in the final sentence?
questions.answer: A believing and accepting attitude is expressed.

questions.question: According to the passage, what can be seen in all things without exception?
questions.answer: A deliberate, wise, and exact order can be seen in all things.

questions.question: What contrast does the passage make between universal things and particular things?
questions.answer: It says both the largest systems and the smallest individual details share the same ordered pattern.

questions.question: Which motions of the earth are mentioned as examples of large-scale order?
questions.answer: Its daily and yearly movements are mentioned.

questions.question: Which small-scale bodily process is mentioned as an example of fine order?
questions.answer: The flow of red and white cells in the blood is mentioned.

questions.question: Why does the passage deny that anything besides the One God can interfere creatively with things?
questions.answer: Because such intentional and wise action requires unlimited power and wisdom.

questions.question: In this argument, what role do created things play?
questions.answer: They serve as places where divine action appears, not as independent creators.

questions.question: Why are knowledge and wisdom necessary for putting things in order?
questions.answer: Because true order aims at meaningful results and benefits, which require understanding.

questions.question: Why are will and choice also necessary?
questions.answer: Because selecting one arrangement over another cannot happen without intention and decision.

questions.question: What does the passage say the visible order of the universe clearly proves?
questions.answer: It clearly proves a single Creator who acts by will and choice.

questions.question: How does the passage explain the shaping of each thing?
questions.answer: Each thing is brought into being, given its state, and shaped in a specific way by divine action.

questions.question: Why are so many natural provisions described as being one?
questions.answer: To show a pattern of unity running through the world.

questions.question: What larger conclusion is drawn from that pattern of unity?
questions.answer: The owner and manager of the world must be one.

questions.question: How does the passage portray the Maker’s relationship to living creatures?
questions.answer: It portrays Him as caring for them generously like honored guests.

questions.question: What do the listed divine Names show by appearing everywhere?
questions.answer: They show that one Lord is acting throughout all places.

questions.question: What does it mean that the Names and acts complement one another?
questions.answer: It means their effects fit together perfectly and support the same unified work.

questions.question: Which divine activity is used as a sample case for this harmony?
questions.answer: The giving of life is used as the sample case.

questions.question: What other actions appear together with giving life?
questions.answer: Creating, shaping, and providing appear along with it.

questions.question: What final truth is established from this harmony of Names and deeds?
questions.answer: That the One indicated by all of them is one, unique, and without partner.

questions.question: What is said about the kind of order found throughout creation?
questions.answer: It is described as wise, exact, and present in everything.

questions.question: What range of examples does the passage give to show this order?
questions.answer: It ranges from the whole universe and the earth’s cycles to facial features, senses, and blood cells.

questions.question: Why is this broad range important to the passage’s message?
questions.answer: It shows that the same truth appears at every level of creation.

questions.question: What does the passage say no being other than the One God can do?
questions.answer: No other being can deliberately and creatively direct itself toward things.

questions.question: If creatures are not independent agents, what are they according to the passage?
questions.answer: They are receivers and places where divine qualities are displayed.

questions.question: What must exist before true order for a purpose can be established?
questions.answer: Knowledge, wisdom, will, and choice must exist.

questions.question: How does the passage connect benefits in creation to divine wisdom?
questions.answer: It says beneficial results show that creation is arranged knowingly and wisely.

questions.question: What does the phrase about varied ordering suggest about the universe?
questions.answer: It suggests that the universe is diverse, yet arranged in a meaningful and controlled way.

questions.question: What three divine qualities are tied to the existence, condition, and form of things?
questions.answer: Power is tied to existence, will to condition, and choice to form.

questions.question: What image is used to describe the world as a place for living beings?
questions.answer: It is described as a place of lodging and care for its living guests.

questions.question: How does the repeated stress on singleness in the world support belief in divine unity?
questions.answer: It shows that the many parts of the world are managed through a unified system pointing to one Lord.

questions.question: What character traits of the Maker come through in the hosting image?
questions.answer: Kindness, generosity, and attentive care come through.

questions.question: What does the passage say about divine Names like the Wise and the Merciful?
questions.answer: Their effects can be seen working in every corner of the world.

questions.question: Besides Names, what two other categories are mentioned as also being one and widespread?
questions.answer: Divine attributes and divine acts are also mentioned.

questions.question: What is the significance of each Name and act being present everywhere?
questions.answer: It shows that divine rule is not limited to one area but covers all things.

questions.question: How are power, wisdom, mercy, grace, and life presented in relation to each other?
questions.answer: They are presented as working together so closely that their effects appear inseparable.

questions.question: What lesson is drawn from the instant appearance of many divine actions in one living thing?
questions.answer: The lesson is that one and the same Lord is acting through all those Names together.

questions.question: What response does the passage model after presenting this proof?
questions.answer: It models faith and wholehearted agreement.

questions.question: What first observation does the passage make about the whole created world?
questions.answer: It observes that every part of it is marked by careful and meaningful order.

questions.question: Which examples show order in the sky and on earth and within people?
questions.answer: The structure of the cosmos, the earth’s repeating motions, and the details of the human body all show it.

questions.question: What conclusion is made about the source of this order?
questions.answer: Its source must be the One with complete power and wisdom.

questions.question: How does the passage treat the idea that created things control themselves?
questions.answer: It rejects that idea and says they are acted upon rather than acting independently.

questions.question: Why does aiming at benefits matter in the argument?
questions.answer: Because aiming at benefits shows intention, not randomness.

questions.question: What human-like capacities are used to explain how order is established, while still belonging perfectly to Allah?
questions.answer: Knowing, willing, and choosing are used to explain it.

questions.question: What does the passage say the ordered universe proves in a way that is plain to see?
questions.answer: It proves the oneness of the Creator who acts by will and choice.

questions.question: How are existence, condition, and form connected to divine action?
questions.answer: Existence comes by power, condition by will, and form by choice.

questions.question: Why does the passage list many parts of the world as single?
questions.answer: It does that to show a repeated sign of unity in the way the world is run.

questions.question: What does that repeated sign say about the Master of the world?
questions.answer: It says that the Master must also be one.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the service given to living beings in the world?
questions.answer: It describes them as being served through many strong and important means.

questions.question: What do those many means of service reveal about the Maker?
questions.answer: They reveal His generosity and care.

questions.question: What are some examples of divine Names mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: Examples include the Wise, the Compassionate, the Giver of Form, the Disposer, the Quickener, and the Nurturer.

questions.question: What is said about the spread of these Names and actions?
questions.answer: Their workings are seen everywhere and fully extend through the world.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the unity among the divine Names and acts?
questions.answer: It describes them as reinforcing one another in a unified pattern.

questions.question: What specific example shows several Names active at once?
questions.answer: When life is given to something, other actions like creating, shaping, and providing also occur immediately.

questions.question: What final proof comes from the same actions appearing everywhere in the same way?
questions.answer: The proof is that their actor is one, single, and unique.

questions.question: How does the speaker respond to that proof?
questions.answer: The speaker says that this truth is believed and accepted.

questions.question: What central feature of creation is emphasized in the opening sentence of the passage?
questions.answer: The central feature is a wise and exact order present in all things.

questions.question: How does the passage show that this order is not limited to one part of existence?
questions.answer: It gives examples from the vast universe, the earth’s patterns, and the smallest details in the human body.

questions.question: What examples from the human body are used to make the argument concrete?
questions.answer: The face, the senses in the head, and the movement of blood cells are used.

questions.question: What kind of being alone can intentionally and creatively affect things?
questions.answer: Only the One who is completely powerful and wise can do that.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the role of all other things?
questions.answer: They receive and display what is done in them rather than creating on their own.

questions.question: Why can regularity aimed at benefits not come from ignorance or accident, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because purposeful regularity requires knowledge, wisdom, will, and choice.

questions.question: What does the visible arrangement of the cosmos prove about its Creator?
questions.answer: It proves that the Creator is one and acts intentionally.

questions.question: What three divine actions are linked with bringing things into existence, giving them a state, and assigning them a form?
questions.answer: Power, will, and choice are linked with those three.

questions.question: What does the world’s description as a hospice or lodging place communicate?
questions.answer: It communicates that the world is a place of provision and care for living beings.

questions.question: Why is the repeated theme of “one” important in that description?
questions.answer: It points to a single Lord behind the unified system of the world.

questions.question: What does the passage infer about the Maker from the way animate beings are served?
questions.answer: It infers that He is highly generous and welcoming.

questions.question: What does the mention of many great servants or officials add to the picture?
questions.answer: It adds a sense of majesty and organized care under one supreme authority.

questions.question: What three groups are named together when speaking about Allah’s activity in the world?
questions.answer: His Names, His attributes, and His acts are named together.

questions.question: What does the passage say about where these are present?
questions.answer: It says they are active in every place and every corner of the world.

questions.question: How do the divine Names relate to each other in their effects?
questions.answer: Their effects fit together and complete one another.

questions.question: What example is given from a living thing to show this combined action?
questions.answer: The appearance of life is given as an example, along with creating, forming, and providing.

questions.question: What conclusion must be reached when the same Names and deeds appear everywhere in the same system?
questions.answer: The conclusion is that the one indicated by them and acting through them is one and unique.

questions.question: What final statement shows the proper response to these signs?
questions.answer: The proper response is faith and assent to this truth.
